title: A Subagent Running a Cheaper Model

turns.userMessage: (subagent task) Find every call site of the deprecated formatCurrency() helper across the repo.
turns.assistantResponse: Searching the codebase for all call sites.
turns.explanation: This subagent runs on a cheaper, faster model (model-a) than the parent session's model-b — a deliberate choice for a narrow, mechanical search task that doesn't need the parent's more capable (and pricier) model. Like any subagent, it has its own isolated context; this first turn writes its own static prefix plus new content.

turns.userMessage: (subagent task, continued) Confirm which call sites pass a currency code and which rely on the default.

toolCalls.name: read_file
toolCalls.argsSummary: full contents of the files matched in the previous search

turns.explanation: Normal cache-building turn within the subagent's own, cheap-model session.

turns.userMessage: (subagent task, continued) Summarize the findings for the parent session.
turns.assistantResponse: 12 call sites found; 9 pass an explicit currency code, 3 rely on the default (which is being removed). Returning a compact summary to the parent.
turns.explanation: Final subagent turn: synthesizes a compact summary that crosses back to the parent. If this same exploration had instead run inline in the parent session under model-b's pricier rates (as in the Inline Exploration Bloat scenario), the equivalent work would cost several times more — isolating it in a subagent saves twice over: once by keeping it out of the parent's permanent cache, and again by letting it run on a model whose rate matches the task's actual difficulty rather than the parent's. This subagent's total spend across all three turns is about 0.0301 AI Credits — cheap because both the isolation and the model choice were suited to a narrow, mechanical search task.
